patterns.title: Catch-22

sources.title: Joseph Heller, Catch-22 (1961), Simon & Schuster publisher page
sources.supports: Literary origin and the exemption request that is treated as evidence of sanity.
sources.boundary: Publisher description of satire; not a clinical source or empirical study. No passage from the novel is reproduced.

sources.title: Cambridge Dictionary, catch-22
sources.boundary: Lexicographic usage, not a formal taxonomy; indexed definition read, direct page intermittently denied automated access.

sources.title: Marco Berti and Ace Volkmann Simpson (2021), The Dark Side of Organizational Paradoxes: The Dynamics of Disempowerment
sources.supports: Restricted agency, power, Catch-22 situations, and limits on challenging contradictory demands; especially manuscript pages 21–22 and 32.
sources.boundary: Conceptual theory drawing on existing research; not a controlled evaluation of the proposed intervention families.

sources.title: Sarah J. Tracy (2004), Dialectic, Contradiction, or Double Bind? Analyzing and Theorizing Employee Reactions to Organizational Tension
sources.supports: Distinguishing forms of organizational tension and the role of restricted discussion in pragmatic paradoxes.
sources.boundary: Qualitative data from two correctional facilities; not evidence that all contradictions are double binds or that discussion guarantees resolution.

sources.title: HSBC UK, No Fixed Address service
sources.supports: Selected-branch service, participating support organizations, caseworker-arranged appointment, and correspondence address.
sources.boundary: Service conditions as checked on 31 October 2026; no universal access or impact estimate.

sources.title: Financial Conduct Authority (7 July 2026), Banks told to improve access to basic accounts
sources.supports: Documented implementation barriers involving basic accounts, non-standard identification, and absence of a fixed address.
sources.boundary: Regulator's report of mystery-shopping findings; not an evaluation of the paid-entry intervention or a general Catch-22 escape method.

patterns.short_description: Recognize when the conditions for obtaining a remedy block that remedy, then identify which rule, evidence requirement, or route would have to change.
use_when: Where can the first accepted experience come from?
Lea seeks a first design job. The employers considered accept only previous paid employment as qualifying experience; no such first role is initially available.
goals: Recognize the familiar predicament before specialist terminology.
Explain the defining mechanism and distinguish neighboring concepts.
Broad everyday circular-prerequisite Catch-22; distinguish Heller’s narrower form where trying to qualify defeats eligibility. Alternative accepted experience would open a route.
Separate hypothetical behavior, model results, documented cases, and practical editorial proposals.
mechanisms: A funded supervised entry assignment is expressly accepted as evidence for later consideration.
The employer must accept the evidence. Supervision costs resources; satisfactory work and a later vacancy are not guaranteed.
example_user_queries: Where can the first accepted experience come from?

visual.question: Where can the first accepted experience come from?
visual.alternative_text: Hypothetical qualitative illustration. Lea needs previous paid experience for a first paid role, while that role supplies accepted experience. A new paid supervised entry route supplies assessed work without demanding prior employment, making later consideration possible. Change: Accept a funded first-entry route instead of requiring prior employment for every start. Limitation: The employer must accept the evidence. Supervision costs resources; satisfactory work and a later vacancy are not guaranteed.
visual.caption: Hypothetical illustration. The familiar job–experience Catch-22 is a circular-prerequisite form. Green marks an accepted first opportunity, not a promise of employment. Paid supervision and a valid assessment are still needed; Heller’s narrower self-disqualifying rule is explained separately.
